title: BLE HID keyboard: a physical-button example

spans.text: The iBle-HID library lets a compatible ESP32 act as a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) keyboard, mouse, or gamepad. This example sends one letter only after a physical button press.
Download the library from [GitHub](https://github.com/ramo828/iBle-HID), place it in
, restart Arduino IDE, and select an ESP32 board. The shared

header exposes the keyboard, mouse, and other HID devices. You do not need NimBLE-Arduino: iBle-HID uses the BLE support included in the ESP32 Arduino core.

send key-down and key-up actions. The library also provides a mouse, gamepad, and combined keyboard+mouse device. These can be used for projects such as a presentation remote or accessibility switch.

The library targets Arduino-ESP32 3.3.11 and later 3.x releases; verify compatibility before using another board/core. See the [English setup and API guide](https://github.com/ramo828/iBle-HID/blob/main/README.en.md).

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: Connect an external button between GPIO 4 and GND; choose an available input pin if your board does not expose it. Select Arduino-ESP32 3.3.11 or a later 3.x core in Arduino IDE. HID is real keyboard input: respond only to deliberate physical user action and test on your own device.
